info.title: Textile RFQ API (v2)
info.description:
Request-for-quote: you name a pair, an exact size, and the wallet
that will settle. Textile asks the market makers online on that
corridor to price it, then returns one firm quote you can execute
(one maker, or several bundled). By default that is every maker on
the corridor; preferred or restricted wallets narrow who is asked.
If nobody covers the full amount, you get a clear no-quote. The
public Swap page uses this same request.
Credentials are optional: present a partner API key, or call
anonymously with a `taker` wallet. Either way, keep the `claimToken`
that /rfq/request returns and send it as `X-Rfq-Claim` on accept,
wallet-stage, cancel, submit, and status. That token is the ownership proof, not the RFQ
id, which every solicited maker receives and which authorizes nothing
on its own.

Makers connect over `WSS /v2/maker/stream` with a maker credential and
an EIP-712 session challenge.

get.description: Whether this task can answer a quote request: it either holds the venue engine lease or knows a holder to forward to. 503 means /v2/rfq/* would fail from here, so the ALB keeps the task out of rotation.

200.description: Venue is serviceable from this task

503.description: No venue engine elected or discovered

post.summary: Enroll a maker by wallet signature
post.description: The bot signs an EIP-712 MakerEnroll with its funding wallet. First connect creates the maker and returns a key. It does not enable any corridor — that happens when the operator confirms the email address they gave. Re-enroll on the same chain rotates only that key slot and returns corridors already enabled. `flagged` is true when Textile has blocked the maker — they get a key but no fan-out. The plaintext API key is returned once.

get.summary: Would enroll accept this OperatorVault for this signer
get.description: Runs the checks enroll applies to a vault funding wallet — registered on Textile's factory, strategy signer equals the signing address, Textile's risk signer, matching execution wiring — and returns every failure as a sentence in `issues`. Empty `issues` means enroll would accept. `orderExecutor` is what the bot should list as `[vault].order_executor`: the active VaultOrderExecutor for a vault with idle yield, else null. Advisory: enroll still runs the real check.

post.summary: Give Textile an email address and get the confirm link
post.description: Maker credential required. The only setup step: confirming the address seats this maker on every RFQ corridor on every chain, now and as more are listed. Posting the same address again resends the link; posting a different one moves where we write to you.

contactEmail.description: An inbox you own. Placeholder and throwaway domains (example.com, mailinator, …) are refused; the rest is proven by the confirm link.

get.description: What the Stitch panel polls after Connect. `corridors` lists the seats on this key's chain and stays empty until `emailVerified` is true; `flagged` true means Textile has blocked this maker.

post.description: Use POST /maker/verify-email. Behaves identically — submits the address and mails the confirm link — and additionally accepts and ignores `contactWhatsapp`, `note` and `corridor`. `accessStatus` is APPROVED once the address is confirmed, PENDING while it is not.

get.description: Use GET /maker/status. Returns the same seats plus an `accessStatus` field: APPROVED once the address is confirmed, PENDING while an address is on file but unconfirmed, NONE before one is given. REJECTED is never returned.

post.summary: Preview a quote from published levels
post.description: Unlocked estimate from the makers' latest published levels. Does not solicit, sign, reserve inventory, or take an outstanding RFQ slot. Amounts can be a few seconds stale. Use POST /rfq/request when the taker commits to a firm, executable quote. Recall-backed depth is considered only when settlementCapabilities includes gmx-recall-v1, just as on the firm request.

get.summary: Price ladder per pair, for aggregators
get.description: For every RFQ pair on the chain, in both directions: the minimum firm sell size, the depth on offer, and indicative points priced the same way as POST /rfq/preview. Each point is exact-input with the fee included: `sellAmount` is what leaves the taker and `buyAmount` is what it receives. Points ascend in both amounts, so a consumer can interpolate between neighbours. Nothing is solicited or reserved. Cached for about 2 seconds.

post.description: No credential required — `taker` is, plus `takerProof`, a short-lived EIP-712 signature by that taker wallet proving the caller controls it (partner keys and admin sessions are exempt). A partner key needs `trades:write`. `preferredLiquidityWallets` / `restrictedLiquidityWallets` are honoured without a credential (a silent drop would price a route the caller did not ask for). Keep the returned `claimToken` — it authorizes accept, wallet-stage, cancel, submit, and status for this RFQ, and is returned exactly once. Blocks while makers are solicited, up to the corridor reply budget: 750ms on most, and up to 10s on one quoted by a custodied signer. On a cold corridor an on-chain token-decimals preflight runs first, budgeted 60s, so the worst-case server-side deadline is ~70s. Set a client timeout above that (75s), not above the budget — a shorter one cancels nothing and discards a quote in flight. Returns a firm, taker-bound signed quote or a no-quote result with a stable reason. Immediate routes include approval and swap calldata. Opt in with settlementCapabilities: ["gmx-recall-v1"] to also allow recall-backed quotes. These initially include only approval calldata: POST /rfq/{id}/accept before acceptBy, then poll status for fresh recall.transactions.swap. The amounts and maximum fee-inclusive debit stay fixed. Recall permits 60 seconds to accept and 90 seconds to settle from request creation; acceptance never extends the signed deadline. An immediate firm quote lives for the corridor quote TTL (60s default); `quote.expiresAt` is the accept cutoff and may be sooner. `taker` is required. `preferredLiquidityWallets` / `restrictedLiquidityWallets`: max 10 each, deduped, mutually exclusive (both → 400); a restricted miss returns reason `no_restricted_liquidity`, never an open-market substitute.

post.summary: Accept a recall-backed firm quote and start preparation
post.description: Only for gmx-recall-v1. Authenticate with X-Rfq-Claim, the original partner in the same environment, or the owning wallet session. Partner keys require trades:write. A foreign RFQ is 404. Idempotent: repeated acceptance reuses the same operation. A first acceptance after acceptBy is 409. Acceptance does not change the firm amounts or settleBy, and does not authorize token spending. Poll GET /rfq/{id} for fresh settlement calldata before wallet submission. Responses use Cache-Control: no-store.

post.summary: Record recall wallet confirmation and submission timing
post.description: Uses the same RFQ ownership and trades:write scope as /accept. Send requested when asking for wallet confirmation, then chain or safe with the returned hash. A Safe proposal hash is not an on-chain transaction or proof of settlement. Report the actual chain transaction through /submit. Repeated reports are idempotent; the same hash may be corrected from chain to safe. Invalid lifecycle transitions are 409. Responses use Cache-Control: no-store.

200.description: Timing recorded; no change to the signed deadline

post.summary: Release a firm quote you requested
post.description: Cancels preparation or tells the selected immediate maker quoteExpired. Only the caller that created the quote can cancel it. A foreign id is 404. Does not un-sign Permit2: signed inventory obligations and outstanding slots remain reserved until consumption or safe expiry. Recall returns its state and awaitingCleanup; an expired quote does not mean its prepared GMX order is immediately cancellable.

parameters.name: X-Rfq-Claim
parameters.description: The claimToken from POST /rfq/request. Required for a caller with no partner key; accepted from any caller as proof it created this RFQ.

200.description: Cancellation recorded; signed backing may remain reserved

post.summary: Report the settlement transaction for a firm quote
post.description: Reports an actual chain transaction; never starts recall preparation. Use /accept first for gmx-recall-v1. A reported hash is not proof of a fill: unknown outcomes remain pending until reconciled. Do not submit Safe proposal hashes.

parameters.name: X-Rfq-Claim
parameters.description: The claimToken from POST /rfq/request. Required for a caller with no partner key; accepted from any caller as proof it created this RFQ.

get.description: Status, routing summary, and terminal fields. Requires RFQ ownership; partner keys need trades:read. Standalone encodedOrder/signature fields are not replayed. For gmx-recall-v1, recall contains preparation state and fresh unsigned settlement calldata when ready (including the original signed order). Poll just before wallet submission; absent recall.transactions means no current calldata is available. Recall responses use Cache-Control: no-store.

parameters.name: X-Rfq-Claim
parameters.description: The claimToken from POST /rfq/request. Required for a caller with no partner key; accepted from any caller as proof it created this RFQ.

rfqClaim.name: X-Rfq-Claim
rfqClaim.description: The claimToken returned once by /rfq/request. Proves ownership of that RFQ only; does not authorize token spending.

apiKey.description: Optional. Partner API key (tx_test_/tx_live_...), or a Textile wallet-session JWT. Omit it to call anonymously against a `taker` wallet. Taker paths only — a maker credential is not accepted here. Keys are environment-scoped: tx_live_ reaches the mainnet corridors, tx_test_ reaches the two testnets with a settlement reactor deployed: BNB Smart Chain testnet (chainId 97) and Base Sepolia (chainId 84532). Any other chainId on a test key is a 400.

makerKey.description: Maker credential issued once by POST /v2/maker/enroll. Bound to one maker and one chain, and distinct from a partner API key — a partner key or wallet session is rejected on the maker paths.

UnsignedTransaction.description: An unsigned EVM transaction to sign and broadcast.

to.description: Approval: the sell token. Swap: the quoted reactor or settlement executor. Use the returned target and quote.spender.

value.description: wei as a decimal string; always "0" for FX swaps

fundingWallet.description: OperatorVault address when the signer is a strategy EOA. Bound in the MakerEnroll EIP-712 digest (equals signingAddress when omitted).

corridors.description: RFQ-capable corridor slugs already enabled on this chain. Empty until the operator confirms their email address.

corridorPairs.description: Same seats as `corridors`, with token addresses so a custom (non-catalog) bot can bind its pool.

flagged.description: True when Textile has blocked this maker. They are not solicited until unblocked.

CorridorPair.description: One RFQ-capable seat, with the tokens a bot binds to.

MakerVerifyEmailSent.description: The link is on its way. Nothing is seated until it is clicked.

emailVerified.description: True only when this address was already confirmed on an earlier link.

sent.description: False when the address was already confirmed, so no new mail went out.

emailVerified.description: True once the operator clicked the confirm link. This is the whole access gate.

flagged.description: True when Textile has blocked this maker. Seats read empty while set.

corridors.description: RFQ-capable corridor slugs enabled on this chain. Empty until the email is confirmed.

requestId.description: The maker id. Access is keyed on the maker now; there is no request row.

accessStatus.description: Derived from emailVerified: APPROVED once confirmed, otherwise PENDING or NONE.

RfqRecallStatus.description: Recall lifecycle for the original firm amounts. Accept within 60 seconds and settle within 90 seconds of request creation. No acceptance or wallet delay extends those deadlines. Unknown broadcasts remain execution-pending until reconciled.

outputAmount.description: Exact customer output, in atomic buy-token units.

maxDebit.description: Maximum fee-inclusive customer debit, in atomic sell-token units.

awaitingCleanup.description: Unsuccessful but backing not yet released. GMX cancellation delay or reconciliation may still block another recall.

transactions.description: Present only for ready/execution-pending while calldata was generated at most 5 seconds ago, its oracle validity has not expired, and settleBy has not passed. Poll again before asking the wallet to submit. Uses the original firm order and quote.spender; never a repriced order.

RfqStatus.description: No standalone encodedOrder/signature. Recall may include fresh settlement calldata containing the original signed order.

sellAmount.description: Once a winner exists, the settled sell-token debit (order output + fee) rather than the requested cap.

buyAmount.description: Once a winner exists, the amount actually delivered.

expiresAt.description: The winning reply's own accept cutoff, not the corridor cap.

lateFillCorrectionClosed.description: True only for FAILED/EXPIRED RFQs after the server's 24-hour late-fill correction window. Clients may retire broadcast recovery once this is true.

chainId.description: Chain the trade settles on. A tx_live_ key may name any mainnet corridor chain; a tx_test_ key may only name 97 (BNB Smart Chain testnet) or 84532 (Base Sepolia), the testnets with a settlement reactor deployed. Anything else is a 400.

sellAmount.description: Exact-input gross spend cap (atomic units). Exactly one of sellAmount / buyAmount. Minimum: the corridor dollar floor (default $1 of notional in the named token, scaled to about $0.01 on the testnets), or the feeable output plus its injected fee when that is larger. Falls back to 1 whole sell token (0.01 on chains 97 and 84532) when the corridor has no usable dollar anchor.

buyAmount.description: Exact-output amount (atomic units). Exactly one of sellAmount / buyAmount. Minimum: the corridor dollar floor (default $1 of notional, about $0.01 on the testnets). Falls back to 1 whole buy token (0.01 on chains 97 and 84532) without a dollar anchor. The protocol fee is charged on the sell-token output, so a floor-sized buy can still get no_valid_quote if that output is dust.

taker.description: The bound settler. Required on POST /rfq/request. Fills are restricted to this wallet for the whole order life. Preview may omit it.

settlementCapabilities.description: Explicit opt-in to recall-backed depth and firm quotes, on both preview and request. Omitted or empty permits immediate settlement only. Recall uses one maker and one order; no mixed bundles. Clients must support accept, preparation polling, and fresh wallet calldata before the fixed settleBy deadline.

includeAttribution.description: Opt in to ERC-8021 tagging of partner swap calldata and the attributionSuffix response field. Omitted or false preserves existing transaction bytes and response fields. Approvals are unchanged. Aggregator keys and non-partner callers remain untagged.

builderCodes.description: Ordinary partner keys only; not applied for RFQ_AGGREGATOR keys, other callers, or /rfq/preview. Used only with includeAttribution: true; builderCodes alone does not enable tagging. Your own ERC-8021 builder codes (e.g. a Base Builder Code), at most 3, each 1-32 characters of a-z, 0-9 and _. The swap transaction comes back with one ERC-8021 tag on the end of its calldata carrying Textile's codes and these, so both programs credit the trade. Pass your codes here instead of appending a second suffix: indexers read only the last tag. Codes starting with textile_ or tp_ are reserved.

flowSessionId.description: Web-only. The Flow session (/v2/flow) this request is the swap leg of. Sent with the session credential in `X-Flow-Access`, it stands in for `takerProof` when `taker` is the session wallet on the session chain — that session was opened with the same signature. A credential that does not vouch falls through to the `takerProof` rules below.

takerProof.description: Proof of control: a TakerControl signature by the `taker` wallet over (taker, chainId, nonce, issuedAt). By default an EIP-712 signature under domain { name: "Textile Taker Control", version: "1", chainId }. The Proof of Funds version the Textile app signs is accepted too, under domain { name: "Textile Proof of Funds", version: "2", chainId } with type ProofOfFunds { purpose: string, wallet: address, chainId: uint256, nonce: bytes32, issuedAt: uint256 } (purpose is the fixed sentence in the authentication guide); the venue tries both, there is no field to pick one; set `scheme` to `eip191` to sign the text rendering instead (see that field). Required on POST /rfq/request unless the caller authenticates with a partner API key or an admin session — or holds a grant: a verified proof covers the same caller naming the same taker on the same chain for ~12h, and requests inside that window may omit takerProof. Treat a 401 proof_of_control_required as the cue to sign and resend (it is answered before any maker is solicited). issuedAt must be within 60s of the venue clock — 5 minutes for an `eip191` proof, since a hardware wallet spends that long paging through the text — and the nonce is bound to this one signed challenge and to the caller that first presented it (the identical proof may be re-sent by that caller while it is fresh; re-binding the nonce, or the same proof from a different caller, is refused as proof_of_control_replayed). EOA signatures verify by ecrecover; smart-contract takers (Safe, 4337) verify on-chain via EIP-1271, including counterfactual accounts through ERC-6492. Missing or bad proof is a 401 with details.reason proof_of_control_required | proof_of_control_stale | proof_of_control_invalid | proof_of_control_replayed; a chain that cannot answer the EIP-1271 read is a 502 with details.reason taker_control_unverifiable (retry the same proof). Ignored on /rfq/preview.

nonceSecret.description: Optional. The 32-byte secret `nonce` is the keccak256 of. With it, a proof signed up to the grant TTL (~12h) ago is accepted, so a Safe or custody wallet whose approvers sign over hours can still request a firm quote. Without it, the usual window. Keep it in the signing client; Safe publishes the signed message, never this.

scheme.description:
How the challenge was encoded before signing. Omit (or send `eip712`) for the typed-data signature described above. Send `eip191` when the wallet cannot sign typed data at all — hardware wallets are the case this exists for — and sign this exact text with personal_sign instead, newline-separated, with the address and nonce lowercased:

Textile Taker Control
Version: 1

Sign to prove you control this wallet so Textile can request a firm
quote for it. This does not approve any transfer, trade or allowance.

Wallet: <taker>
Chain: <chainId>
Nonce: <nonce>
Issued at: <issuedAt>

The Proof of Funds version uses its own header and body (see the authentication guide); the venue tries both. Both encodings bind the identical fields and must recover to `taker`; the scheme is an encoding choice and grants nothing. The one difference is the validity window: an `eip191` proof is accepted for 5 minutes rather than 60s, because issuedAt is fixed before the device prompt opens and a Ledger paginates this text over seven screens. Everything else — nonce binding, grants, EIP-1271 — is the same.

RfqFeedState.description: Present only when the corridor’s price feed is not fresh: the state of the market rate makers quote off. Makers stop quoting on a stale or degraded feed, so this is usually why a no_quote came back. Informational: it never changes the answer. On /rfq/preview it can also come with a priced answer, when a maker quotes outside market hours (wider, smaller) or quotes a clamped price (wider). On /rfq/request it is sent with no_quote only. Describes the feed, never a maker.

status.description: market_closed: the feed follows a market with trading hours and it is closed (or opened within the last 15 minutes and the first prices are still coming in). stale: the feed has not updated and there is no schedule to explain it. degraded: the feed is fresh but flagged as held, clamped or a fallback. A clamped price is a live one that moved more than its per-minute limit and was held to it; makers that support it keep quoting it, wider. Held and fallback prices take makers dark.

market.description: market_closed only. colombia_fx: Colombia’s interbank FX spot market, Mon–Fri 08:00–13:00 Bogotá (UTC-5), closed on Colombian public holidays.

opensAt.description: market_closed only: when the next session opens. In the past for up to 15 minutes after an open.

availableSellAmount.description: Packed published sell-token depth after the min-slice floor.

reservedUntil.description: no_quote only: a recent firm quote is holding the liquidity THIS request would have used, until this time, so the book reads thinner (or empty) than the maker really is. The hold runs to the signed order deadline plus a 30s clock-skew buffer, or until a reconciled fill. Cancelling the quote or letting its accept window lapse does not end it early, because the signed order stays executable. Scoped to the request: a reservation on the opposite direction (it locks the maker’s balance of your buy token, not the other one), or one held by a funding wallet outside a restricted list (inventory is per Permit2 owner, and one maker may register several wallets), is not reported. Absent when nothing relevant is reserved — that no_quote is a genuinely empty book, not a race.

retryAfterMs.description: no_quote only, alongside reservedUntil: milliseconds to wait before re-previewing. Already includes the slack for the venue to release the reservation and the maker to republish. Retrying sooner re-reads the same reserved book.

claimToken.description: Ownership credential for this RFQ, returned exactly once, here. Send it as X-Rfq-Claim on accept, wallet-stage, cancel, submit, and status. The original partner in the same environment or owning wallet session can also prove ownership. The rfqId alone authorizes nothing. Store the claim with the quote.

route.description: Present on recall quotes only; immediate responses keep their existing shape.

availableSellAmount.description: no_quote only, when the request named sellAmount: packed published depth on the sell token. Omitted when zero. If this is below the requested size, retry at this amount.

availableBuyAmount.description: no_quote only, when the request named buyAmount: packed published depth on the buy token. Omitted when zero.

reservedUntil.description: no_quote only: a recent firm quote is holding the liquidity THIS request would have used, until this time, so the book reads thinner (or empty) than the maker really is. The hold runs to the signed order deadline plus a 30s clock-skew buffer, or until a reconciled fill. Cancelling the quote or letting its accept window lapse does not end it early, because the signed order stays executable. Scoped to the request: a reservation on the opposite direction (it locks the maker’s balance of your buy token, not the other one), or one held by a funding wallet outside a restricted list (inventory is per Permit2 owner, and one maker may register several wallets), is not reported. Absent when nothing relevant is reserved — that no_quote is a genuinely empty book, not a race.

retryAfterMs.description: no_quote only, alongside reservedUntil: milliseconds to wait before asking again. Already includes the slack for the venue to release the reservation and the maker to republish. Retrying sooner re-reads the same reserved book.

latestOrderDeadline.description: Latest signed-order deadline in the bundle — the last instant any slice is still executable. Equals orderDeadline for a single-maker quote.

spender.description: Contract the taker must approve and the returned swap targets. Equals reactor on an ordinary quote. May instead be VaultOrderExecutor for Aave or the GMX recall executor. Always approve this quoted address. Recall swap calldata arrives later in status; the spender and firm debit do not change.

orders.description: Every signed order in the quote. One maker when a single quote covers the size; several when the venue bundled makers. Recall always has one order. Execute the returned swap calldata; for recall, accept and fetch fresh recall.transactions.swap from status first.

transactions.description: Send approval first (skippable if allowance covers takerPays). Immediate quotes also include swap. Recall quotes initially include only approval; accept and poll status for recall.transactions.swap.

attributionSuffix.description: Returned only when includeAttribution is true; otherwise omitted. ERC-8021 hex suffix, already appended to transactions.swap.data. Null for aggregators, sessions, and anonymous callers. Safe relayers append it to the fully encoded execTransaction payload; ERC-4337 integrations append it to final UserOperation.callData before estimation and signing. Requires wallet suffix support and an indexer for that payload. Do not append it twice to a direct transaction.

details.description: Structured detail, when the error has a machine-readable form. Branch on this rather than on `message`, which is prose and can be reworded.

reason.description:
Stable reason code.
`corridor_unavailable` (400): this pair cannot be quoted over RFQ — either no corridor exists for it on that chain, or the corridor is still in BOOK mode. Route the taker to /v1 or another pair.
`insufficient_funds` (400): the named taker does not hold enough of the sell token. Carries atomic `required` / `available`, plus `committed` when the taker's other live quotes are what spoke for the balance.
`proof_of_control_*` (401): the `takerProof` was missing, stale, from the wrong wallet, or replayed. Sign a fresh challenge.
`taker_control_unverifiable` (502): the EIP-1271 read for a smart-account taker failed. The proof is still good — retry with the same one.

required.description: `insufficient_funds` only: atomic sell-token units the request needs.

available.description: `insufficient_funds` only: the taker's raw sell-token balance, atomic.

committed.description: `insufficient_funds` only, and only when the wallet could fund this request alone: atomic sell-token units already reserved by the taker’s other recent quotes. Wait for one to expire, or execute it. Cancelling a quote does not release its hold early.

reservedUntil.description: `insufficient_funds` with `committed` only: when enough of those holds lapse for this request to fit (signed deadline plus a 30s skew buffer). Absent when no lapse would be enough.

retryAfterMs.description: `insufficient_funds` with `reservedUntil` only: milliseconds to wait before asking again.
